vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: to go around a new place to discover what is there
beautiful to look at, especially nature and views
the plan of a trip, day by day
the amount of money you plan to spend
a boat that carries people and cars across water
the line where the land meets the sea
to tell someone that something is good and they should try it
a high place where you stop to see the view

paras: In three weeks my sister and I are going to fly to Split, and I still cannot believe it. Our itinerary is almost ready. We are going to spend the first four nights on the coast, and then we are going to drive north to Ljubljana. My friend Marta lived in Croatia for six years, and she recommended two things: never book every day, and always take the slower road.

So that is what we are going to do. On the second morning we are going to take the ferry to one of the islands and stay until the evening. On the fourth day we are going to drive the scenic route along the coastline instead of the fast motorway. It takes two hours longer, but Marta says the view is worth every minute. There is a lookout point above one of the villages, and I am looking forward to sitting there with a coffee and doing absolutely nothing.

The rest is open on purpose. We have a small budget for food, so we are not going to eat in the tourist places near the gates. We are simply going to explore, and we will decide at lunchtime where to eat. I have no idea what to expect from Ljubljana, but everyone tells me the same thing, so I am sure it will be a good surprise.

bank.label: Useful sentences to talk about a plan
items: We are going to spend four nights on the coast.
I am really looking forward to exploring the islands.
I plan to take the slower road, because the view is better.
The ferry is full? Then I will take the bus instead.
I have no idea what to expect, but I am sure it will be good.
A friend recommended a small place near the harbor.
Our budget is not going to cover a hotel on the water.
At the end of the month we are going to drive north to Ljubljana.

items.situation: Someone asks: 'What are you going to do in Croatia?' Answer with two planned activities.
Your friend says the ferry is full on Tuesday. Decide something new right now.
Say one thing you are looking forward to, and remember the -ing.
tips: I am really looking forward to ...

items.situation: A local asks how long you are staying and what you want to see. Answer both.
tips: We are going to stay for ...

items.situation: Predict one thing about Ljubljana, a city you have never seen.
Ask a local for a recommendation for someone with three days there.

listenings.text: Good morning, and welcome aboard. This ferry is going to leave in about ten minutes, and the crossing takes fifty five minutes. If the sea is calm we will arrive a little earlier. The upper deck is open, and I recommend it: the view of the coastline as we leave the harbor is the best part of the trip. There is a small cafe downstairs, but it only takes cash today. The last ferry back tonight leaves at nine, so please do not miss it. Enjoy the crossing.

So you have three days here. Here is what I would recommend. On the first day, do not plan anything at all. Just explore the old town on foot and let it surprise you. On the second day, take the early ferry to the island, because after eleven the boats are full of people. And on the third day, drive the scenic road north. There is a lookout point about twenty minutes out of town, on the left, with no sign and no bus. Most visitors never find it, and it is the view you will remember.

extra_audio.text: First they are going to fly to Split at the end of August. Then they are going to spend four nights on the coast. On the second morning they are going to take the ferry to one of the islands. On the fourth day they are going to drive the scenic road along the coastline. Finally they are going to arrive in Ljubljana with nothing booked at all.
